reason: The cited evidence confirms that rapid quenching yields an amorphous structure and that slower cooling produces multiple crystalline phases, but it provides no data on reheating protocols, crystallization kinetics during heating, or the effect of heating rate on amorphous retention. The key premises about ultra-fast reheating suppressing crystallization and entropy stabilizing the amorphous state during heating are unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Ultra-fast reheating can kinetically bypass nucleation and growth of primary crystalline phases
High configurational entropy (partly from phosphorus) stabilizes the amorphous state during fast reheating
Rapid quenching (10^5–10^6 K/s) yields an amorphous structure in this alloy
Slower reheating allows primary crystallization and multistep crystallization events
A critical reheating rate threshold exists above which crystallization is suppressed
